newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan c/a surplus declining more slowly--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan c/a surplus declining more slowly--MOF.

text.p: Japan's current account surplus is sitll on a declining trend although the pace is slower, a Ministry of Finance official said on Monday.

Although the current account outlook will depend largely on currency rates, oil price movements and global economies, growth in imports continues to exceed that of exports, and the deficit in services trade is expanding, he said.
"Although the pace of the declines in the current account surplus is slowing down, the shrinking trend remains unchanged," he said.
He added that the ministry did not think the current account surplus will return to a rising trend in the coming months.
The official attributed the difference in the November customs-cleared trade figures and current account trade figures to the method of calculating aircraft imports.
The customs-cleared trade surplus rose 0.2 percent in November year-on-year, while the trade balance in the current account posted a 3.4 percent drop in November.

The customs-cleared data counts aircraft imports at the time the the actual aircraft arrives in Japan while the current account figures include it at the time the contract is made. The customs-cleared figures also include shipping costs while the IMF-based or current account data does not include these.
As a result, the value of imports in the current account trade data were around 30 billion yen higher than the customs-cleared trade data.
The official said the increase in the deficit in services trade was due to more people travelling abroad.
